A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GaSLight work. All 11 pages of each, including equations, six tables, eight figures, and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original HDR estimation and relighting evaluations, comparisons and ablations in Tables 3–6, and application demonstrations in Section 5.

after.justification: v4 retains the original quantitative evaluations and ablations in Tables 3–6, alongside qualitative relighting and application results.

M1.justification: Recursive diffusion-based exposure prediction, HDR merging, and InstantSplat-based HDR Gaussian reconstruction retain the same procedures and losses. Numbering the existing Gaussian Splat subsection does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: The panorama training collection, Si-HDR and BtP-HDR benchmarks, landscape subset, two PanoHDR-NeRF scenes, and application scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains LDR, HDRCNN, MaskHDR, SingleHDR, ExpandNet and Exposure Diff. The GlowGAN comparison in Table 4, PanoHDR-NeRF comparisons in Tables 5–6, and Ours+LaNet variant in Table 6 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The protocols retain the same 113-image filtered Si-HDR evaluation, 23-image landscape subset, rendering conditions, metrics and model settings. The PanoHDR-NeRF comparison still uses the vanilla LANet model.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the manual HDR-clamping consistency test in Figure 6 and the LaNet replacement ablation in Table 6. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-evaluation run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 retain every numerical result and ranking, and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 3's relighting MSE for Ours remains 0.0131 on Si-HDR and 0.0041 on BtP-HDR.

T1.justification: The exposure definitions, recursive prediction relations, HDR-merging weights and sampling distributions are unchanged. Neither version contains theorem or proof developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same method, dataset, novelty, performance and application claims, including spatially varying HDR Gaussian lighting and accurate bright-source estimation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning white-balance-related errors and consistency regularization are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning unseen lighting, multiview consistency, complex light transport, real-time rendering and large scenes.

D1.justification: Data capture, augmentation, training, hardware and inference details are identical, including 415k training iterations and 20 diffusion steps. The code-availability statement and project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 72 references and research-positioning passages appear in both PDFs. No cited work or substantive relationship to previous HDR, NeRF, Gaussian-splat or lighting methods changes.

P1.justification: The existing Gaussian Splat lighting representation paragraph heading becomes numbered subsection 3.2. Other edits concern capitalization and the version stamp; the prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 5 moves from the upper-right to the middle-left portion of page 6, with accompanying text reflow. Figure 5 capitalizes 'ours' as 'Ours'. All tables and figures retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: v4 gives the existing Gaussian-splat stage its missing subsection number, matching Figure 3's Section 3.2 reference and clarifying the two-stage method structure. This provides a small presentation benefit; the scientific evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged.
